key_insight: Recognizing updated medical guidance did not ensure faithful incorporation: the primary model recognized 90.8% of revisions but fully incorporated only 58.5%.
clinical_relevance: Clinical LLM outputs may retain outdated recommendations even when updated guideline evidence is available.
method: Introduced ChronoEvo with 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 types of medical knowledge change.
Evaluated recognition and incorporation across 14 models, with two-clinician adjudication of 300 responses.
Tested a revision-salience intervention to emphasize updated guidance.
evidence_signal: The primary model showed a 32.3-percentage-point recognition–incorporation gap; clinician-adjudicated validation found a 40.3-point gap.
watch_item: Emphasizing revisions reduced outdated content and improved clinical correctness, but did not significantly improve full incorporation.
paper_title: Large language models show systematic failures in incorporating evolving medical knowledge
